You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

The patch addresses a bug where pending packets in nfqueue could hold stale references to conntrack-related objects (zone templates, timeout policies, helpers) upon their removal. To prevent this, it calls `nf_queue_nf_hook_drop(ctx->net)` in three destroy functions to drop such packets before the objects are freed:

- **`__nft_ct_set_destroy`** (for `NFT_CT_ZONE`): drops packets referencing conntrack zone templates, which use a percpu area that can be removed.
- **`nft_ct_timeout_obj_destroy`**: drops packets using conntrack timeout policies that are being removed.
- **`nft_ct_helper_obj_destroy`**: drops packets using conntrack helpers that are being removed.

Additionally, the patch adds `#include "nf_internals.h"` to provide the declaration of `nf_queue_nf_hook_drop`.

All modifications share the same purpose: ensuring no enqueued packets hold dangling references, thus avoiding potential use-after-free or crashes.

Based on your summary and the commit message in the patch, you need to:

1. analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 
2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>mutex_lock(&nft_ct_pcpu_mutex); (in case NFT_CT_ZONE of __nft_ct_set_destroy)</text>
<text>nf_ct_untimeout(ctx->net, timeout); (in nft_ct_timeout_obj_destroy)</text>
<text>nf_conntrack_helper_put(priv->helper4); (in nft_ct_helper_obj_destroy)</text>
Reason:
<text>These statements remove conntrack zone templates, timeout policies, and helpers without first dropping packets enqueued in nfqueue. Such packets may hold references to these objects, leading to stale references and potential use-after-free or crashes.</text>

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>nf_queue_nf_hook_drop(ctx->net); (added before mutex_lock in case NFT_CT_ZONE)</text>
<text>nf_queue_nf_hook_drop(ctx->net); (added before nf_ct_untimeout in nft_ct_timeout_obj_destroy)</text>
<text>nf_queue_nf_hook_drop(ctx->net); (added before nf_conntrack_helper_put in nft_ct_helper_obj_destroy)</text>
Reason:
<text>These calls drop any packets enqueued in nfqueue that might hold references to the conntrack objects about to be removed, ensuring that no stale references remain after the removal, thus preventing use-after-free or crashes.</text>
